competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample asks outright for an area and names the square unit in the question itself: seed 44 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' resolves by 3x3=9, and seed 604 'A rectangle has sides 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' by 8x5=40. Nothing here asks the pupil to do anything beyond computing the area of a stated square or rectangle, which is the verb this competency uses.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four sub-cases the wording names are present. Square in sq cm: seed 502 'A square has a side of 4 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'. Square in sq m: seed 45 'A square has a side of 5 m. What is its area in sq m?'. Rectangle in sq cm: seed 605 'A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 6 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'. Rectangle in sq m: seed 606 'A rectangle has sides 4 m and 7 m. What is its area in sq m?'. Neither shape nor unit is left unsampled.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The stems are two short sentences carrying one multiplication and no unit conversion, e.g. seed 46 'A rectangle has sides 6 m and 2 m. What is its area in sq m?' keeps both lengths in the same unit as the requested answer. Seed 601 is the only multi-clause item and its extra load is concrete and countable, 'with square tiles that are 1 m on each side'. That is the right reading and reasoning demand for the start of Grade 3.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Seeds 50 and 500 render the same stem word for word, 'A square has a side of 4 m. What is its area in sq m?', with the same answer 16 and the same four option values merely reordered; seed 502 repeats that computation in centimetres as 'A square has a side of 4 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'; seeds 44 and 501 are likewise a side-of-3 pair. Thirteen of the fourteen samples are one of just two fixed frames, the square-side frame and the rectangle-sides frame, with only the numbers and the unit swapped.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 601 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 2 m long and 3 m wide with square tiles that are 1 m on each side.' asks for a count of tiles, and its answer 6 carries no square unit, so the single contextual item in this packet reports a tile count rather than an area stated in sq cm or sq m; the identical item also stands in the sibling problem-solving node. The other thirteen samples, such as seed 602 'A rectangle has sides 4 m and 3 m. What is its area in sq m?', sit squarely on this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every sample demands exactly one multiplication of two one-digit lengths and no division at all: seed 42 'A rectangle has sides 4 cm and 3 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' is 4x3=12, seed 43 is 3x5=15, seed 45 is 5x5=25, and the three largest products are seed 604 at 8x5=40, seed 605 at 5x6=30 and seed 606 at 4x7=28. All sit inside the basic multiplication facts and no result passes 40, which is plausible for Grade 3 Quarter 1.
